summary.headline: Prince Pipes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% to INR850 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR110 crore on 23% volume growth; management guides 11-13% margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly volumes of 62,167 MT (+23% YoY), with revenue of INR850 crore (+18%) and EBITDA of INR110 crore (+100%, 13% margin). Management attributed the quarter to aggressive pricing, pass-through of inventory gains to channel partners, product mix (CPVC, PPR) and absence of inventory losses, which had hurt the first nine months. FY26 revenue grew 3% to INR2,598 crore, volume rose 8% and EBITDA rose 43% to INR232 crore (9% margin). Management guided to 11-13% annual EBITDA margin and 12-15% annual volume growth, while flagging April destocking and a weak channel in April before a May revival.

financial_highlights.value: Revenue INR16 crore; loss INR5 crore

segments.name: Plumbing and drainage (PVC, CPVC, PPR, HDPE)
segments.commentary: Plumbing and drainage is about two-thirds of the portfolio. CPVC is the fastest-growing polymer, followed by PVC, PPR and HDPE, with CPVC volume growth above company average.

segments.name: Agri pipes
segments.commentary: Agri is less than 30% of revenue and more price sensitive; management said demand was healthy but building material drove the tailwinds.

segments.name: Bathware (Aquel)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue of INR16 crore and loss of INR5 crore. Breakeven targeted at INR20-25 crore quarterly revenue, expected in Q2-Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Share of value-added products in revenue was 23-24% in FY26, targeted at 27-28% in FY27. DECILO low-noise PP pipe was launched in Q4 with in-house manufacturing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected in 11-13% range on an annual basis; quarterly results may swing with inventory gains or losses, which management expects to be range-bound.
FY27 volume growth guidance of 12-15%; management said aspiration is higher.
FY27 capex of INR200-210 crore, covering maintenance, debottlenecking at two or three plants, and the second tranche of Bhuj (Bathware).
Targeted FY27 capacity utilisation of about 58-60% if 15% volume growth is achieved.
Long-term target gross asset turnover of about 2.5x (currently about 1.5-1.6x), reached over the long term at 60-65% utilisation.
Debtor days to be reduced by a further 10-15 days by end of FY27 (about 50 days now).
Inventory to stay within the 65-75 day range (raw material plus finished goods).
Bathware breakeven targeted at INR20-25 crore quarterly revenue, expected Q2-Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR200-210 crore, including maintenance, debottlenecking at 2-3 plants, and Bhuj second tranche; about INR40-45 crore relates to completion of the April acquisition.
Overall production capacity utilisation about 52% in FY26; Bihar (Begusarai) plant at about 60%; South plants underutilised.
Installed capacity about 435,000 MT; debottlenecking is limited to certain product categories at a couple of plants.
Bhuj (Gujarat) facility acquired from Klaus Waren Fixtures via asset purchase (phase two completed) to serve as dedicated Bathware manufacturing base.
Capex includes warehouse and storage upgrades at plants to ramp inventory in lean periods.
demand_pricing: Q4 volume growth was robust across January, February and March; management said the 23% quarterly growth is not sustainable, partly due to restocking in March.
April was weak industry-wide due to channel destocking after March restocking; May saw a strong primary pickup and demand revival in the first 15 days.
Prince passed inventory gains to channel partners in March; Q4 inventory gain was close to zero. Management says pricing is at par with market leader in PVC and CPVC on a pan-India average.
Competitive intensity reportedly lower due to consolidation; smaller players facing supply issues and losses. Company added distributors, including in white-space markets in South and East India.
Retail to project mix about 70:30; projects were about 25% of revenue around 1.5-2 years ago.
Plumbing demand reported as good across urban and rural areas; management sees no postponement despite sharp real estate cost escalation.
Raw material mix: payables driven by import versus domestic buying (suppliers include Reliance, Chemplast and imports from North America and Japan).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and volume guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 11-13% annual EBITDA margin and 12-15% annual volume growth, with quarterly variation possible from inventory gains or losses.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance include Bathware losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said the 11-13% EBITDA margin guidance includes Bathware losses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins improve so sharply and can they sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited no inventory loss (versus large losses in the first nine months), record volumes of 62 kt improving cost absorption, and stronger mix from CPVC and PPR.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation about 52% overall; Bihar about 60%. FY27 capex INR200-210 crore. Utilisation target 58-60% if 15% volume growth is achieved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory in the 65-75 day range; debtor days about 50 (from 60) with a further 10-15 day reduction targeted in the next four quarters. Payable days depend on import versus domestic mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bathware breakeven path?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 revenue INR16 crore and loss INR5 crore. Breakeven at about INR20-25 crore quarterly revenue, targeted for Q2-Q3 FY27, with no change in spend.

qa_highlights.question: Has Prince lost market share over the last three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed this, saying growth was slower than some peers but always above industry average, and that the company is back on track in recent quarters.

risks_watch: Inventory gains and losses from PVC/CPVC price volatility; April 2026 showed destocking and price correction after a March price increase.
Sustainability of the 23% Q4 volume growth given restocking; management itself said it is not sustainable.
Bathware losses (INR5 crore in Q4) and the breakeven timeline of Q2-Q3 FY27.
South plant underutilisation and whether share gains in South materialise to lift utilisation.
Payable days surge (cited by an analyst) and dependence on imports versus domestic raw material.
Agri demand is price sensitive; real estate cost escalation could affect building material demand.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q4 volumes, margins and consolidation-led share gains, but cautious on near-term demand, saying 23% growth is not sustainable and April was weak. Management was less specific on the per-kg margin, distributor counts and incentive quantum, deferring some of these to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: So in Q4, inventory gain was, I would say, close to zero, because it was passed on to the channel, which is why we were able to deliver a 23% kind of a volume growth.
So I think by next year, we should hit 27%, 28%.
We have done around INR16 crores in fourth quarter.
So we have seen many such cycles. And I think a few players tried to pass on cost overnight, which we felt was not the right strategic decision.

adds.what: Bhuj (Gujarat) facility acquired from Klaus Waren Fixtures via asset purchase, phase two completed; second tranche of Bhuj Bathware capex included in FY27 plan
Debottlenecking at 2-3 plants (limited to certain product categories) within FY27 capex of INR200-210 crore

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume growth of 12-15% (aspiration higher) and 11-13% EBITDA margin, backed by distributor additions, value-added/DECILO launch and a lower-competition environment, plus FY27 capex of INR200-210 crore for debottlenecking and Bhuj Bathware; however, no specific new capacity with numbers is quantified and utilisation is only 52%, so backing is partial.
